newsitem.title: USA: U.S. presses for more talks on Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. presses for more talks on Cyprus.

text.p: The United States pressed on Monday for a second round of U.N.-sponsored talks on Cyprus following "positive and useful" discussions last week.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns, referring to the talks in New York between Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot leaders, said: "We're very pleased they took place. We think that face-to-face dialogue on the issue of Cyprus is quite important. In fact, it's essential.
"And the United States would certainly support a second round of talks if that can be agreed to. We hope very much it will be agreed to," he told a news briefing.

Secretary-General Kofi Annan's special adviser on Cyprus, Diego Cordovez, led four days of talks between President Glafcos Clerides, who is also head of the Greek Cypriot community, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
The talks at a secluded rural retreat called Troutbeck, 90 miles (145 km) north of New York City, ended on Saturday.

"We know that President Clerides and Mr. Denktash have known each other for 47 years. They hadn't met in three-and-a-half years and it's essential they continue to meet face-to-face for the cause of peace," Burns said.

At the United Nations, Cordovez said the two sides had agreed in principle to a second round of talks in Switzerland, beginning on Aug. 11. Another source said that session might be held near Montreux.
U.S. negotiator Richard Holbrooke did not attend the U.N.-sponsored talks but he met Clerides on Monday morning and later was to have talks with Denktash.

Holbrooke will travel to Europe, including London, in two weeks to consult with allies on Cyprus. Burns said Holbrooke would not travel to Cyprus or to the eastern Mediterranean until at least after the next round of talks.

Holbrooke "feels it's not appropriate for him to visit Cyprus or Greece or Turkey at the present time, because we want to support the United Nations. And if there is to be a second round of discussions in Europe in August ... then Dick feels he ought not to get in the way of that," Burns said.
